mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust corporate hiring and rising consumer spending, which directly supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring any specific threshold condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that typically precedes stronger corporate profit growth and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE is below 4.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: The joint expansion of labor market strength (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) creates a virtuous cycle where rising employment fuels higher disposable income, leading to increased consumption and corporate revenue growth, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between PAYEMS and RSAFS is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the combined signal fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.0% and the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) is at or above 2.0%, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy environment with persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs and reduced consumer spending pressure equity valuations.
failure_condition: In periods meeting the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS>3.0% and CPIAUCSL>=2.0%), the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and business investment, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring any specific threshold condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth is positive (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1,000,000 units annually (1000.0 in thousands of units), it signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST exceeds 1000.0, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 3.5% in a single month, it signals an aggressive monetary tightening that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher rates dampen economic activity and equity valuations.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 3.5% in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a robust economic expansion that typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days without requiring any specific threshold condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).
